title: Private Deploy: Mirror-based Artifact Bootstrapping, Upgrade Sequencing, and Deterministic Fallback Protocol
creator: Aisha Verma
description: This ticket defines requirements and acceptance criteria for a mirror-driven artifact distribution and upgrade fallback protocol for Private/VPC (air-gapped and limited-egress) deployments. The goal is to allow sites with restricted egress to safely bootstrap images and upgrades from a validated mirror, perform staged canaries inside isolated networks, detect divergence or corruption, and execute deterministic rollback or offline remediation without requiring wide open egress or manual artifact re-transfer.
requirements: Mirror discovery and validation: Private operator can configure one or more internal mirrors (HTTP(S)/OCI registry) with explicit base-URLs and TLS fingerprints. The agent must validate mirror TLS and artifact checksums before use.

Immutable manifest signing: All production images and manifests must be signed by Redwood's artifact signing key; private operator mirrors must preserve and expose signature metadata for verification during bootstrap and upgrade.

Staged upgrade sequencing: Support three phased rollouts within a private site: control-plane canary (single node), regional canaries (subset of nodes), and broader pool rollout with configurable pause windows and automatic health gates.

Offline checksum promotion: Operators can pre-seed a mirror with an allowlist of artifact checksums and a signed promotion token; agent will refuse to fetch or apply artifacts not present in allowlist for fully air-gapped installs.

Deterministic rollback: Upgrade orchestration must record a deterministic rollback plan (exact image hashes and configs) and provide an automated rollback action that can be executed without external network access.

Network partition simulation: Provide tooling (local CLI + operator steps) to simulate partial partition scenarios used during canary validation so teams can assert graceful degradation and fallback behavior before production upgrades.
Minimal egress policy: Define explicit minimal egress endpoints necessary for non-air-gapped operators; support a zero-egress mode where all artifacts are sourced from pre-seeded mirrors.

KMS/HSM rotation compatibility: If KMS rotation is requested during upgrade, provide an offline-compatible rotation path that ensures keys used to verify signatures remain available or are bundled with the mirror promotion token.

Observability hooks: Upgrade must emit deterministic events to local audit logs (and optional mirrors of logs) with artefact hashes, signature validation result, and canary health snapshots for post-upgrade forensics.
Operator playbook: Provide an operator-facing upgrade playbook that includes preflight checks, expected durations, manual escalation paths, and rollback triggers for the on-prem SRE team.
Backout time budget: Default upgrade sequence must include a configurable backout budget (e.g., 15 minutes) for each canary stage after which automatic rollback triggers if health gates fail.
acceptance_criteria: Given a private site with a seeded internal mirror, the agent can perform a control-plane canary upgrade using only mirror-sourced artifacts; all artifacts validate signatures and checksums before apply.
Given a mirror with a modified artifact (checksum mismatch), the upgrade must fail fast and log a clear error that includes expected vs observed checksum and signature verification status.

Given zero-egress mode enabled, the system must refuse to fetch artifacts from external endpoints and must proceed only if artifacts are present in configured mirrors and present in the allowlist token.

A deterministic rollback plan is created and stored locally before any node is upgraded; executing the rollback plan without network access returns the cluster to the exact pre-upgrade image hashes and config within the documented backout budget.

Canary health gates (resource metrics, start-time, readiness probe success, error-rate) are defined and enforced; if any gate fails during a canary stage within the backout window, the system auto-rolls back and emits an audit event with metrics snapshot.
Network partition simulation tooling exercises the same health gates and demonstrates rollback behavior under simulated node isolation; results are recorded in local logs for review.
Upgrade orchestration records artifact signatures and exposes them in local audit logs in a machine-readable format (timestamped entries with hash and signer ID) for post-mortem verification.
KMS rotation during upgrade either completes using offline-compatible tokens provided in the mirror or the upgrade is blocked with a clear remediation path documented in the operator playbook.

The operator playbook is present in the console (or packaged with the release tarball) and includes step-by-step commands, expected timelines, and contact points for escalation; at least one customer-facing PMC has validated the playbook in a staging environment.
notes: Focus on minimizing human-in-the-loop requirements while preserving safety for highly regulated sites. The design must assume adversarial mirror states (e.g., checksum mismatch) and provide explicit failure modes and operator remediation steps.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Mirror compromise or stale mirror content could push bad artifacts. Mitigation: mandatory signature verification, allowlist promotion token, and preflight checks rejecting unsigned artifacts.
Risk: Operator error during mirror seeding. Mitigation: provide a validation CLI that checks artifact hashes and signs a local manifest when seeding is successful.
Risk: Automatic rollback may not suffice for latent data migrations. Mitigation: block destructive migrations by default and require explicit operator opt-in with documented compensation steps.
Risk: Long-running rollbacks under partition could breach SLA. Mitigation: define backout budgets and fail-open policies configurable per-customer with explicit risk acknowledgement.
out_of_scope: Design for multi-region cross-account mirroring across public clouds (this ticket targets single-site private/VPC deployments).
Full automation for physical media provisioning (physical media fallback is covered by a separate initiative).
open_questions: What is the canonical format for the signed promotion token (JSON Web Signature, custom envelope)?
Should signature verification accept an operator-managed root CA chain in addition to Redwood's signing key for customers who require full key ownership?
What telemetry can be safely exported for hosted observability without violating airgap constraints (e.g., aggregated anonymous metrics vs. none)?
Do we require an offline manifest signing CLI that runs inside the customer's network, or is a hosted signing service with exported signatures acceptable in air-gapped installs?
